Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 +0000
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: MVP success slate: token-econ, SLOs & owner assignments

Sara — thanks again for a productive discovery today. Quick recap and a proposed "MVP success slate" that we can treat as the acceptance criteria for the POC. Please review and confirm or flag changes.

POC duration: 6 weeks (see proposed milestones attached). We can move to an 8-week schedule if Nimbus needs more ops/time (Ben comments below).

Proposed acceptance criteria (MVP success slate):
- Latency: P95 generation latency < 250ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), P95 < 450ms for long prompts (<=1024 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 150 QPS for steady-state traffic; ability to handle 250 QPS short bursts for 1–2 minutes.
- Cost: target incremental inference cost <= $0.0025 per token when using recommended batching/quantization config.
- Quality: automated eval on your sample prompts — >= 90% pass rate on label match and intent accuracy; no more than 3% hallucination on the high-risk prompt set.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and graceful fallback to smaller model variant if latency or capacity issues detected.

Operational/acceptance tests we will run:
- 3-tier latency sweep (short/medium/long prompts) against representative traffic.
- Throughput ramp to verify autoscaling and batching behavior.
- Token-cost model verification based on your sample traffic.
- Quality snapshots using the 200-case evaluation harness you shared (or similar).

Owners (initial):
- Redwood PM (Jordan): overall POC coordination, success criteria acceptance.
- Redwood Infra (Ben): infra config, model selection, runtime tuning, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated).
- Redwood QA (Marissa): eval harness, quality gating, runbooks.
- Nimbus Product (please confirm owner): provide sample traffic, decision-maker list, and access to any internal test environment.

Attachments: POC-outline-v1.pdf, sample-prompts.csv (attached).

Actions / next steps:
1) Nimbus to confirm product owner and handoff of sample prompts/datasets by EOD Friday.
2) Redwood to provide a 6-week milestone plan and a short SOW addendum for the POC (DocuSign link to follow).
3) Schedule a short 30-min kickoff next week to align on test windows and data handling.

If this looks good I’ll circulate a slightly expanded schedule and the DPA addendum.

—
Jordan Blake

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our internal priorities. A couple of notes and a request: 

1) Throughput: our production projection is closer to 200 QPS sustained with 350 QPS short bursts during peak windows. Is the 250 QPS burst you listed a hard ceiling or can Redwood support the 350 QPS burst if we size the POC accordingly?

2) Product owner: loop in Michael Chen (michael.chen@nimbus.ai) — he will be the decision owner for acceptance criteria and will coordinate datasets.

3) I uploaded an anonymized 1k-sample dataset and a short usage pattern doc to the Drive folder you shared. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-POC-materials

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 12:40:00 +0000
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@nimbus.ai>
Subject: Re: MVP success slate: token-econ, SLOs & owner assignments

Appreciate the recap — a few practical notes from infra/ops side after reviewing the sample dataset: 

- Capacity & burst: Redwood can support a 350 QPS short burst if we allocate a temporary higher-capacity pool (Dedicated burst) for the peak windows. That will change the cost profile for the POC; I’ll include delta estimates in the schedule.

- Cost target: to reach the ~$0.0025/token target we should test a mixed strategy: 8-bit quantized model variant + continuous batching with a 25–50ms batching window. Expect cost variance by prompt length; we’ll attach a token-cost runbook to the schedule.

- Latency tests: we’ll create three acceptance tests (short/medium/long). For fairness we’ll define fixed prompt lengths (64 / 256 / 768 tokens) and run 10 sustained-minute windows at target QPS. P95 thresholds will be measured per-window.

- Deployment options: two POC deployment models: Hosted (fastest to start, lower tail control) or Dedicated (predictable latency + isolation). Recommend starting Hosted to validate quality & token economics and then run a 48-hour Dedicated smoke test in week 4 if the quality numbers look good.

- Timeline: I recommend an 8-week POC (2 weeks ops prep + 4 weeks tests + 2 weeks stabilization/evidence collection) given your burst needs — Jordan, if Nimbus prefers 6 weeks we can compress but will need parallel workstreams.

Owners (updated):
- Ben Carter: infra sizing, cost model, smoke tests.
- Marissa Cole: eval harness, quality thresholds, regression checks.
- Jordan Blake: cadence, executive readout, decision sign-off.

I attached a refined schedule (POC-schedule-v2.xlsx) with cost deltas and a short checklist of what we need from Nimbus to start (API keys, test accounts, SLA contact).

Next steps: I’ll publish an ops prep checklist by EOD and propose two kickoff windows next Tue/Wed.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
